newsitem.title: GERMANY: German private TV sees stronger Q1-Nielsen.
newsitem.headline: German private TV sees stronger Q1-Nielsen.

text.p: German private television stations reported 8.3 percent growth in net advertising turnover for the first quarter of 1997, Bauer publishing group said on Thursday.

During the same period, public networks posted a 4.8 percent drop in turnover in 1996, Bauer said, based on figures provided by Nielsen S&P Werbeforschung. Nielsen S&P compiles advertising data, which it provides to media clients.

German industry spent about 6.3 billion marks on advertising in the first quarter of 1997, Bauer said, of which roughly three billion marks went to print media and nearly 3.2 billion to electronic media.

Those results reflected a 0.7 percent dip in advertising income for print media, while electronic media saw a 6.8 percent climb in turnover during the first three months of the year, Bauer said. Radio increased its take by four percent to 387 million marks.

In print media, newspapers were among the losers, posting a 5.8 percent drop in turnover to 1.3 billion marks. Magazines boosted their ad sales by 4.2 percent during the same period to 1.46 billion marks, Bauer said.
Bauer said erotic magazines and periodicals for teenagers saw particular growth, along with television guides and women's magazines.
Billboards only drew 128 million marks during the period, representing a decrease of 16.3 percent.
